claims.claim: CE-Replay keeps design-dependent control executable and is neither learned nor a complete-design response table.
The experiments use the documented floor-based q-error objective without retrospective modification.
Recurring maintenance is represented by a generic function; mechanism-weighted count is an empirical instantiation rather than a universal coefficient.
The workload-scale solver provides neighborhood-local, not global, optimality.
Statistics-set inclusion may be non-monotone and candidate effects are contextual.
The supported MCV predicate boundary includes validated scalar predicates and constant IN/=ANY, not arbitrary predicates.
MCV GreedyCover maximizes currently unestimated dimensions, prefers fewer statistic keys, and uses PostgreSQL order for remaining ties.
Overlapping statistics can suppress later applicability, while disjoint statistics can contribute in later rounds.
CE-Replay executes native payload-dependent MCV numerical combination rather than a learned correction factor.
Supported ScalarArray predicates are evaluated directly against MCV items with ANY/IN OR semantics; duplicates do not multiply item frequency.
FD uses a distinct aggregated dependency program rather than MCV GreedyCover.
MCV executes first and passes consumed-clause state to FD, making the composition directed.
CE-Replay is workload-specialized and source-informed, but is not an automatic PostgreSQL partial evaluator/compiler.
Payload schema/key order is semantically meaningful.
The semantic boundary is PostgreSQL 16.14 supported conjunctive base-restriction MCV+FD with bounded ScalarArray support.
The objective oracle is exact only with respect to validated replay semantics and the supplied frozen realization.
Safe incremental evaluation requires structural/counterfactual as well as realized dependency.
Fresh semantic replay error and frozen-to-fresh payload drift are different quantities.
Final cross-workload optimization searches selection under fixed recorded precedence.
Greedy initialization recomputes contextual benefit per maintenance unit after each accepted addition.
The local solver enumerates feasible ADD/DROP/SWAP moves, chooses deterministic best improvement, and terminates when none improves.
Small/restricted exhaustive audits do not imply full-instance global optimality.
Semantic dependencies permit exact audited incremental move evaluation, while reduced control replay need not reduce wall time.
CE-Replay reduces exact move-evaluation work but does not change the combinatorial worst case.
Offline candidate payload acquisition is assumed and is distinct from recurring deployed maintenance.
